newsitem.title: UK: Sears demerges Selfridges, sells Freemans.
newsitem.headline: Sears demerges Selfridges, sells Freemans.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc on Tuesday announced a restructuring of the troubled conglomerate including the demerger of its profitable Selfridges department store.

The group also said it had conditionally agreed the sale of its Freemans mail order arm to Littlewoods for 367.5 million pounds ($596.9 million) and said it intended to return the net proceeds to shareholders.

"We have now conditionally agreed the sale of Freemans to chairman Sir Bob Reid said in a statement. "Following completion of the sale, which is expected in the late summer, we intend to return the net proceeds to shareholders".
David James has been appointed executive chairman of the loss-making British Shoe Corporation to develop a programme to achieve best value for the footwear division.

It anticipates this will be "substantially" achieved in the next year and said if disposal was the best way forward it would take that route. The group said it had already received interest from a number of parties.
The restructuring of the group means that the role of group chief executive disappears and as a consequence Liam Strong will leave the group.

The demerger of Selfridges is expected to take place during 1998. Sears reported annual pre-tax profits before exceptional charges of 88.9 million pounds against 70.8 million the previous year, while maintaining its dividend at 3.95 pence per share. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
